summary: Iter 10 — Procurement pack ZIP endpoint (backend) + primary/secondary CTAs on /trust (frontend) fully validated. Backend: 7/7 pytest passed. Frontend: both CTAs trigger downloads with correctly-formatted filename; ZIP is 88531 bytes; page sections + status pills render; 0 console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: Content-Disposition uses date stamp YYYYMMDD (e.g., 2026...) but frontend anchor.download uses YYYY-MM-DD. Effective filename is driven by the anchor.download attribute in the browser (frontend) so tests saw 2026-07-05 with dashes. Consider aligning both to a single format for consistency (harmless today).
downloadProcurementPack has no try/catch around fetch failures — a network error will silently keep the loader off but no user-visible error toast. Minor UX polish.
PDF renderer is compute-heavy (~1-3s for 4 PDFs). If procurement pack becomes hot path, cache the ZIP for the day since content is deterministic per date.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Procurement pack endpoint /api/trust/procurement-pack works. Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/test_procurement_pack.py can be reused as regression. Filename verification pattern: ITHR-Academy-Procurement-Pack-YYYY-MM-DD.zip (from frontend anchor) or YYYYMMDD (from Content-Disposition header).
